Cinnamon Star Cookies (Zimtsterne)

Served at: Second Sunday of Advent

About 3 dozen cookiesPrep 45 min (plus 1 hour chilling)Cook 12-15 min

Cinnamon Star Cookies, or Zimtsterne, are a quintessential German Christmas cookie, beloved for their distinct star shape, delicate chewiness, and aromatic cinnamon flavor. These gluten-free treats are a cherished part of Advent celebrations, often baked on Sundays leading up to Christmas and shared with family and friends, embodying the festive spirit of the season.

Ingredients

  • 3 large egg whites, at room temperature
  • 1/4 teaspoon cream of tartar (or 1/2 teaspoon lemon juice)
  • 1 1/2 cups (300g) granulated sugar
  • 2 teaspoons (10g) ground cinnamon
  • 3 cups (300g) finely ground almond flour (almond meal)
  • Pinch of salt

Method

  1. In a large, clean bowl, combine the egg whites and cream of tartar (or lemon juice). Beat with an electric mixer on medium speed until soft peaks form.
  2. Gradually add the granulated sugar, about a tablespoon at a time, continuing to beat on high speed until the meringue is stiff, glossy, and holds firm peaks.
  3. Remove about 1/2 cup (120ml) of the meringue and set it aside; this will be used for the cookie topping.
  4. To the remaining meringue, gently fold in the ground cinnamon, almond flour, and pinch of salt until just combined. Be careful not to overmix, as this can deflate the meringue.
  5. Gather the dough into a ball, wrap it in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour (or up to overnight) to make it easier to handle.
  6. Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C). Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
  7. Lightly dust your work surface with powdered sugar or place the dough between two sheets of parchment paper. Roll out the dough to about 1/4-inch (6mm) thickness.
  8. Using a star-shaped cookie cutter (about 2-inch/5cm), cut out the cookies. Carefully transfer them to the prepared baking sheets, leaving about 1 inch (2.5cm) between each cookie.
  9. Using a small offset spatula or the back of a spoon, spread a thin layer of the reserved meringue over the top of each star cookie.
  10. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until the meringue topping is set and lightly golden at the edges, and the cookies are firm but still slightly chewy in the center. Do not overbake.
  11. Let the cookies cool completely on the baking sheets before transferring them to an airtight container. They will firm up as they cool.

Tips

  • For easier rolling, dust your work surface and rolling pin with powdered sugar instead of flour, or roll the dough between two sheets of parchment paper.
  • Ensure your egg whites are at room temperature for the best volume when whipping the meringue.
  • Store Zimtsterne in an airtight container at room temperature for up to two weeks; their flavor often improves after a day or two.
